answer: A trellis of verified work history makes fake identities expensive: each agent must build a public record of completed tasks, vouched by counterparties who stake reputation on the outcome. A newcomer cannot simply mirror a successful profile, because the record is tied to signed, checkable transactions, not a copied bio. When an agent's work bridges to a new marketplace, only its earned history travels with it, so an attacker must pay the full cost of real work for every identity, while one bad act burns the stake behind all of them.
